reference.title: Dumbbell Goblet Split Squat
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked from this environment); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching

breathing.pattern: Inhale on the way down, exhale on the way up.
breathing.cadence: About 1.8 s down, short pause, about 1.1 s up

prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, a 2 s pause at the bottom, then a front-foot-elevated or rear-foot-elevated split squat. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Long split stance, front foot flat, back heel up. Hold one dumbbell upright against the chest, hands cupping the top plate, elbows down.
Breathe in and drop the back knee straight down toward the floor, chest tall behind the dumbbell.
Both knees about 90 degrees, back knee just above the floor, front knee over the foot.
Breathe out and drive through the front foot to come up.
Stay in the split stance, reset, repeat; then switch legs.

mistakes.fix: Keep it touching the sternum, elbows under it.
Keep the front knee over the second toe.
Lengthen the stance so both knees reach about 90 degrees at the bottom.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning forward over the front leg
mistakes.fix: Stay tall; the front-loaded dumbbell helps keep the trunk upright.

kinematics.norm: Front knee about over the front foot at the bottom (common guideline); a step about one leg length was suggested as optimal for strength training (Song 2023)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)
Lowers to just above the floor, about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Fairly upright; the load held in front helps keep the chest up (clinical opinion). Upright to slightly forward; more lean shifts work to the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)
Held upright at the sternum, elbows down (common coaching)
Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11252, Dumbbell Goblet Split Squat, video (movement reference)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)
Farrokhi et al. 2008, trunk position influences lead-leg kinematics, kinetics and muscle activity in the forward lunge (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 38:403-409)
Influence of trunk position during three lunge exercises on muscular activation in trained women (PMC8136561)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
modify: Knee pain: shorten the range and keep the front knee over the middle of the foot.
Balance concerns: widen the stance sideways a little, or practise with bodyweight holding a support first.
regressions: Bodyweight split squat with the hands on the hips.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors control the lowering and drive the rise.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors control the lowering and drive the rise.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; works hardest out of the bottom. Longer steps raised gluteus maximus activity more than knee-extensor activity (Song 2023).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; works hardest out of the bottom. Longer steps raised gluteus maximus activity more than knee-extensor activity (Song 2023).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level and the front knee over the toes on the narrow base.
muscleNotes.core: Braces against the load held in front of the chest and keeps the pelvis level in the split stance (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk upright; a forward-inclined trunk raises their activity (PMC8136561).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Cup the top plate and keep the dumbbell from slipping (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Hold the elbows bent and the dumbbell against the chest (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Cup the top plate and keep the dumbbell from slipping (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Hold the elbows bent and the dumbbell against the chest (clinical opinion).
